title: He Told 5 AIs: Make Money or Get Deleted
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

idea.name: Five-model AI-managed investment portfolio competition
idea.one_liner: A self-directed investor gives five AI models equal portfolios, follows their weekly stock and ETF recommendations, and seeks investment returns.
idea.customer: The guest as a self-directed investor; no external customer is stated.
idea.offer: Five competing AI-selected portfolios with weekly buy and sell recommendations.
idea.revenue_model: Potential capital gains or dividends on invested funds; no customer revenue is stated.

claims.claim: The guest began the experiment about six months earlier.
claims.quote: So, I started like 6 months ago or or maybe a little less uh using the different AI models to manage my money.

claims.claim: He invested $1,000 with each model.
claims.quote: So, I decided to give five different models $1,000 of real money.

claims.claim: He considered using only $50, but thought he might neglect an experiment with such a small stake.
claims.quote: I didn't want to do it like 50 bucks cuz then I was thinking, well, maybe I would just neglect it or whatever.

claims.claim: He put in $5,000 in total.
claims.quote: So, 5,000 bucks I put in.

claims.claim: His AI subscriptions cost at least $20 per month each, but he already used them for work.
claims.quote: I have at least a $20 a month subscription, which with each of the five since I use all five for work anyway, that wasn't like an additional expense.

claims.claim: He framed the competition around retaining a $20 monthly subscription.
claims.quote: I was just trying to see if robots powers that be would act in their best interests to keep my $20 subscription a month to them.

claims.claim: He said $20 or $50 stakes would not make the experiment feel serious.
claims.quote: If it's 20 bucks, 50 bucks, then you're not going to take it seriously.

claims.claim: He gave a hypothetical example of Grok up 5% while Claude was up 35% after the first month.
claims.quote: So what it could be doing is let's just say that over the first month Grock was up 5% and Claude was up 35%.

claims.claim: He reported that Claude had more than doubled his money.
claims.quote: So, Claude's more than doubled my money already.

claims.claim: A friend suggested putting in $50,000.
claims.quote: he's like, "Ah, why didn't you put 50 grand in?"

claims.claim: He said he could not lose more than the $1,000 invested with any one model, though he was getting close to that loss.
claims.quote: I mean, luckily, I can't lose more than $1,000 of from any given model, but I'm getting close.

claims.claim: One model had lost money while the other three had made money, and the portfolios were nearing twice the original $5,000 overall.
claims.quote: and one has lost and the other three have made money, but I'm getting close to doubling the the original 5K overall.

claims.claim: He said Gemini bought about $500 of a 2x Solana stock.
claims.quote: So, it bought like $500 of that Salana 2X stock.

claims.claim: He said Gemini sold that holding for $162.
claims.quote: And it sold it at 162 bucks.

claims.claim: He described the Solana-linked product as moving at twice the cryptocurrency's movement.
claims.quote: So Salana is a cryptocurrency and there's a thing that whatever Salana does, this thing does two times that.

claims.claim: He described another ETF as doing three times the movement of the stocks it holds.
claims.quote: It's a ETF that does three times whatever the stocks in it do.

claims.claim: He reported that the Intel holding was up 285%.
claims.quote: You know, you would have thought, but it is up 285% on what it put in on the Intel buy.

claims.claim: He said Claude's Intel investment grew from about $120 to $550.
claims.quote: So, it put in it put in like 120 bucks in Intel and now that 120 is at 550.

claims.claim: He planned to run the experiment for one year.
claims.quote: I said I was going to do it for one year.

claims.quote: They all started with a,000 bucks real money. Gemini is at $445.

claims.claim: At the reported snapshot, Grok had $1,451 and was up 45%.
claims.quote: Grock is at $1451. So, it's up 45%.

claims.quote: Perplexity is at $1,731 and Chetch is at $1,739.

claims.quote: So, they're up 70% and they both own currently only they both own SOL, that semiconductor triple leverage one.

claims.claim: He said Claude's $1,000 had grown to $2,400.
claims.quote: So, 1,000 has gone to 2400.

claims.claim: He said his total $5,000 had grown to about $7,800.
claims.quote: So, in total, my 5,000 is like $7,800.

claims.claim: He reported the S&P up 5%, the AI portfolios up 60%, and Claude more than doubled.
claims.quote: S&P's up five. My AI group together is up 60 and Claude is more than doubled.

claims.claim: The host summarized the AI portfolios as outperforming the market by 12 times.
claims.quote: So overall, you've 12xed the market.

ideas.delivery: The guest prompts five AI chat models, sends them screenshots of holdings on a weekly cycle, asks for buy or sell decisions, and manually places trades through his Charles Schwab brokerage account.

prices: At least $20 per month per AI subscription
